key_insight: BenchX shows that tumor-detection AI can look strong overall while failing in small, rare, and demographically underrepresented subgroups.
clinical_relevance: This benchmark highlights the need to test medical imaging AI beyond average accuracy so clinicians and developers can better identify hidden bias and reliability gaps before deployment.
method: Built an open benchmark using 85,355 CT scans.
Evaluated 12 tumor-detection AI models across tumor size, location, patient subgroup, and imaging protocol.
Used LLMs to extract and organize subgroup information from clinical data for scalable analysis.
evidence_signal: The study systematically benchmarked 12 models on 85,355 CT scans and found poorer performance in rare or underrepresented groups, including young, female African Americans.
watch_item: Subgroup findings may be sensitive to label quality, dataset coverage, and the challenge of validating very rare cases with limited annotated data.
paper_title: BenchX: Benchmarking AI Models for Cancer Detection and Localization with Demographic and Protocol Biases
